audit.whatIsWrong: This side's chart gave Yone five of seven rows and the prose says he owns levels 1-5 outright. The already-audited mirror (nautilus__yone) sets levels 2, 3 and 4-5 to Nautilus, First item to Skill and 2+ items to Yone. The two pages currently answer 'who wins Level 2' differently.
audit.why: 50.89% over 7942 games is a coin flip, not a five-row Yone lane. Mechanically Nautilus holds levels 2-5: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield, Riptide is 5-7s of repeated slow, and Staggering Blow roots on his first auto, so a step-up Yone cannot walk out of. Yone's edge arrives with items.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 3 and 4-5 set to Nautilus and First item to Skill, matching the mirror exactly, with the four whys and four phases[].why lines rewritten so the prose no longer claims Yone owns those levels.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item row was written as an unconditional Yone spike; nothing acknowledged that Nautilus's CC still decides the fight at that point.
audit.why: Blade of the Ruined King raises Yone's damage but does not answer a hook plus root plus Depth Charge chain, which is why the mirror rates that row Skill.
audit.corrected: First-item spike restated as a real but conditional window, gated on Dredge Line's 10-14s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two content fields told the player to eat or dodge Nautilus's hook 'with Windwall timing'. Yone has no Wind Wall — that is Yasuo. Fate Sealed was again described as setting up knockups; it is a blink behind the last champion in a line plus a pull. Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide and Depth Charge were all referenced without a single cooldown or range.
audit.why: Riot ability text in the brief. Telling a Yone player he can block a hook with a wall he does not own is the kind of error that loses a game outright.
audit.corrected: Windwall references removed and replaced with the real counterplay — Dredge Line is a 1150-range projectile you sidestep or break line of sight against. Fate Sealed restated as blink-behind-and-pull. Cooldowns added: Dredge Line 10-14s, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, Riptide 5-7s, Depth Charge chasing from 825 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'track Dredge Line' everywhere but never gave the number, so 'engage on its cooldown' had no clock.
audit.why: 10-14s is long enough to be a real window; Titan's Wrath at a flat 12s is the second one worth poking off.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].t.

edits.before: Level 2 stays yours; you shove and poke while he has no way to punish your aggression.
edits.after: Level 2 is his: Titan's Wrath shields the trade and Riptide slows you out of it.

edits.before: Level 3 remains yours — his hook is his only tool and dodging it leaves him helpless in lane.
edits.after: Level 3 stays his — Riptide on 7s plus the passive root chains every step-up you take.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 favour you as your damage and mobility fully outclass a tank with no waveclear.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his — Riptide's slow drops to 5s and his shield covers each trade.

edits.before: First item is yours as your DPS shreds his pure-tank build while he can only try to peel.
edits.after: First item is a skill window: your DPS ramps but his CC still decides the fight.

edits.before: W shield-grit covers every exchange you start. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath shields every exchange on a flat 12s. Take the trade only after he has spent that shield.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but so is Riptide on 7s — his slow plus the passive root outlasts a step-up you cannot walk out of.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Riptide falls to 5-6s here, so his slow covers the gap between hooks. Trade only in Dredge Line's 10-14s downtime and farm safe.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind him and pulls; Depth Charge chases you 825 units and stuns. Whoever ults second wins the level 6.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike, but his CC still decides it — force only when Dredge Line is on cooldown.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Nautilus carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind their back line and pulls it to you — build your teamfight around that. Nautilus carry threat: 7/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 10-14s and 1150 range — commit only in its downtime.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield — poke it off before you commit.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto per target and starts the chain.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Q3-R him.
edits.after: Dredge Line is a 1150-range projectile on 10-14s; Depth Charge chases and stuns. Fight in that gap.

edits.before: You stay ahead — even a full-tank Nautilus is just a body you kite with E and cleave down, and his single hook is your only real threat, easily dodged or eaten with Windwall timing.
edits.after: You stay ahead — a full-tank Nautilus is a body you kite with Soul Unbound and cleave down, and Dredge Line is the one threat: a 1150-range projectile, so sidestep it or break line of sight.

edits.before: You remain favoured into items and beyond: a tank Nautilus is a kite target for your E and Spirit Cleave, and his lone hook threat is trivial to dodge or Windwall. He'll try to matter in fights, not in a sidelane 1v1.
edits.after: You remain favoured into items and beyond: a tank Nautilus is a kite target for Soul Unbound and Spirit Cleave, and his hook is a 1150-range projectile you sidestep — Yone has no windwall to eat it. He matters in fights, not a sidelane 1v1.

notes: TWO REAL ERRORS: the content layer twice told a Yone player to eat or dodge Dredge Line 'with Windwall timing'. Yone has no Wind Wall — that ability belongs to Yasuo — and following that line means standing in a hook. Both instances replaced with sidestep / line-of-sight counterplay. Chart aligned to the already-audited mirror; see questionsForUser, because this side's packet chart disagrees with the mirror.
